unit.subject: English
unit.unitOverview: In this unit you will learn the words for places in a town — the shop, the market, the school, the hospital and the library. You will learn about the people who work in these places, and the words that tell us where something is: near, far and next to. You will meet the traffic lights too, and learn that red means stop and green means go. A town is full of helpful places and kind people, and we all help to keep it clean and safe.
unit.learningPath:
Begin with the guided teacher launch and learn a few words through pictures and play.
Listen to the Unit story and join in with repeated language.
Complete six language, speaking, early-writing and practical activities.
If you have access to live teacher sessions, meet your teacher three times each week for two weeks for extra practice — these are optional, and every skill in this unit is also fully covered through the teacher launch, story, and speaking and writing activities above.
Finish the ten-question checkpoint, then tell an adult what you can do if one is nearby — or say it out loud to yourself.

readings.title: A Walk Around Town
readings.theme: town places, helpful people, safety and care
readings.setting: Home, online lesson or Grade 1 classroom
readings.passageScript: One sunny morning, Amal held her mother's hand. “Today we will walk around our town,” said Mum. “Come and see!” First they came to the big road. The traffic lights were red. “Red means stop,” said Amal. They waited. Then the light was green. “Green means go!” said Amal, and they walked across. “Look, Mum! There is my school,” said Amal. Her big brother Adam waved from the gate. “Hello, Amal!” he called. “Hello, Adam!” said Amal. She smiled. Next to the school was the market. It was very busy. A kind man was selling sweet mangoes. “Good morning,” said the shopkeeper, Omar. “Would you like a mango?” “Yes, please,” said Amal politely. “Thank you!” Omar smiled. “You are a polite girl,” he said. They walked past the hospital. “The doctor, Faduma, works here,” said Mum. “She helps people when they are sick.” “Doctors are kind,” said Amal. Near the park, Amal saw some litter on the ground. A little boy named Leo was dropping his paper. “Oh no,” said Amal. “Please put your paper in the bin. We keep our town clean!” “Sorry,” said Leo. He picked up the paper and put it in the bin. “Thank you for helping,” said Amal. Now the park was clean and pretty. Last of all, they came to the library. It was quiet and calm. “This is a special place,” said Mum softly. Amal's grandma was there. “Come, my dear,” she said, and gave Amal a warm hug. On the way home, Mum asked, “What did you see in our town today?” Amal counted on her fingers. “I saw the school, the market, the hospital, the park, and the library! I saw kind people too.” “And what did you learn?” asked Mum. Amal smiled a big smile. “Red means stop, green means go — and we all help to keep our town clean. I love my town!”

grownUpGuide.label: Teacher & Parent Guide
grownUpGuide.intro: In this unit, your child learns the words for places in a town — the shop, the market, the school, the hospital, the mosque. They learn the people who work in these places, and simple words that tell us where things are (near, far, next to). They also meet the traffic lights and learn that red means stop and green means go. The big idea is that a town is full of helpful places and kind people, and that we all help keep our town clean and safe. The goal is warm, confident English — not perfect spelling.

sections.title: 🧭 About this unit (please read first)
sections.body:
Your child is a beginner, about 5–7 years old, and is just starting to read. So YOU lead this unit — a teacher in class or a parent at home.

Work in short, happy sessions of about 15–20 minutes. Lots of pointing, saying, singing, colouring and playing — very little writing.

This guide tells you what to do. The Child Activity Sheet is what your child draws and colours. The Story is one you read aloud.

This is the LAST unit of Year 1. Take a moment at the end to celebrate everything your child has learned this year!

sections.title: 💬 Using the AI Tutor with a young child
sections.body:
The grown-up holds the device and reads with the child — do not leave a 5-year-old alone with it.

Ask the tutor to say a place word slowly so your child can copy the sound: “Please say the word ‘hospital’ slowly.”

Ask it to play a town game: “Ask my child where the doctor works.”

Ask it to sing the traffic-lights rhyme, or to give one more simple activity if your child wants to keep going.

sections.title: 🌟 Tips for teaching absolute beginners
sections.body:
Keep it short and playful. Stop while it is still fun.

Repeat, repeat, repeat — young children learn by hearing words many times.

Use your hands, face and voice. Point, act, and smile.

Praise every try. Confidence matters more than being correct at this stage.

sections.title: Songs and Rhymes
sections.body:
“The Traffic Lights” — say it together

Red means STOP. / Green means GO. / Yellow means WAIT, / Even if you're late.

Hold up a red thing, then a green thing. Freeze like a statue on “STOP” and march on the spot on “GO”. Say it three times — a little louder each time!

“I Live in a Town” — a happy song

I live in a town, yes I do, / I live in a town, yes I do, / Made by many kind hands, / All together built this town!

Clap along and name a place in your town after each line: “the market!”, “the school!”, “the mosque!”

sections.title: How to Teach This Unit, Step by Step
sections.body:
Repeat this simple shape over several short sessions:

1. Warm-up (2–3 min)

Greet your child: “Hello! Where do we go today?”

Sing the traffic-lights rhyme with actions.

2. Learn the words (5 min)

Point to a picture of a place and say it clearly: “the market”. Ask your child to repeat.

Do 4–5 places at a time. Use big smiles and lots of praise.

Add a position word: “The shop is next to the school.” Point as you say it.

3. Play and sing (5 min)

Traffic Lights game: “Green!” — your child walks; “Red!” — your child freezes.

Town Walk: pretend to walk to a place. Ask “Where are we going?” Child says “To the ______!”

Sing “I Live in a Town” and name a place after each line.

4. Story time (5 min)

Read the Story file, “A Walk Around Town”, aloud. Point to the places and ask the simple talk-about questions.

5. Activity sheet (5 min)

Sit with your child and do one or two activities from the Child Activity Sheet. Read each instruction aloud for them.

6. Wrap-up (2 min)

Ask: “Where did we go today?” Celebrate! Say “Well done!” and one thing they did well.

sections.title: Sentence Patterns to Say Out Loud
sections.body: Speaking comes before writing. Practise these spoken patterns often:
items: “I go to the ______.” (school, market, mosque)
“I can see a ______.” (shop, park, bus)
“The ______ is next to the ______.”
“It is ______.” (big, small, busy, clean)
“Red means stop. Green means go.”

sections.title: Simple Check — What to Look For
sections.body: You do not need a test. Just watch and tick when your child can do these:
items: Points to and names 5 town places.
Names 2 people who help us (teacher, doctor…).
Says where a place is: “next to”, “near”.
Says what red and green traffic lights mean.
Says one thing: “I go to the ______.”

sections.title: 🎉 Well done — your child has finished Year 1!
sections.body:
This is the last unit of Year 1. What a journey! Your child started as a brand-new beginner and can now name many English words, join in songs and rhymes, and say simple sentences out loud.

Take time to celebrate. Look back at their drawings from earlier units and let them show you what they can say.

In Year 2, your child will build on all of this — reading a little more, writing a little more, and speaking with more confidence. They are ready!

From all of us at Ehel Academy: well done to your child, and well done to YOU for teaching with love. 🌟
